# ATR - Agentic Test Runner

> AI-powered test runner that analyzes failures and runs browser-based behavior tests

## What is ATR?

ATR is a command-line tool that:
1. Executes shell commands and uses AI to analyze failures
2. Runs browser-based behavior tests written in natural language
3. Provides an HTTP server for programmatic browser control

## Key Commands

### Test LLM connectivity
```bash
atr test    # Verify LLM backend is configured and accessible
```

### Run commands with AI failure analysis
```bash
atr run --cmd "go test ./..."
atr run --cmd "npm test" --context "Running auth tests"
```

### Run browser behavior tests
```bash
atr run --behavior tests/login.test.txt
atr run --behavior tests/e2e/ --browser-url http://localhost:3000
```

### Browser server mode (for AI agents)
```bash
# Start browser daemon
atr browser start

# Navigation
atr browser navigate <url>
atr browser back
atr browser forward
atr browser reload

# Interaction
atr browser click <target>    # target: text, element ID (e0), or CSS selector
atr browser fill <target> <value>
atr browser hover <target>
atr browser press-key <key>

# Inspection
atr browser snapshot          # Get interactive elements with UIDs
atr browser screenshot        # Capture screenshot
atr browser url              # Get current URL
atr browser title            # Get page title
atr browser html             # Get page HTML
atr browser eval <script>    # Run JavaScript

# Page management
atr browser new-page [url]
atr browser list-pages
atr browser select-page <index>
atr browser close-page <index>

# Debugging
atr browser console          # Get console messages
atr browser network          # Get network requests
atr browser errors           # Get failed requests

# In-page agent HUD (headed browsers only; for a human at the keyboard)
atr browser start --hud      # Start headed with the agent panel showing
atr browser hud on           # Or turn it on later
atr browser hud off

# Stop browser
atr browser stop
```

### Filling passwords without leaking them

The HUD agent has a `browser_fill_secret` tool that takes a field and either a
configured `ref` or a `command`. ATR runs the command and types the output
straight into the field; the value is never returned to the model.

Never fetch a credential with `execute_command` and pass the result to
`browser_fill` — tool results join the message history and are re-sent to the
provider on every later turn, so one fill would put the password in every
subsequent request.

Configure named refs in `~/.atr/config.yaml`:
```yaml
secrets:
  refs:
    github/password: "pass show github/password"
```

## Browser Server Architecture

For AI agents, ATR provides HTTP server mode:

```
AI Agent --> atr CLI --> HTTP --> ATR Server --> Browser
```

- Daemon runs in background with state at ~/.atr/browser.state
- Commands output human-readable text by default
- Use --json flag for structured output
- Browser always runs in visible (non-headless) mode
